summary: PDL from the Triton pre-attention kernel into the B=1 stream-K kernel is rules-safe: only key seq_b-1 is written by the primary, and the hypothesis defers that tile plus q until after griddepcontrol.wait. With no explicit trigger in the primary, though, the overlap is limited to the launch gap and roughly meets the 1 us kill bar. Time an explicit early-trigger variant too, and split the q load out of the first tile's cp.async group.
justification: Mechanism: full decode_1 is 22.6 us of shape against 1.4 + 18.6 us of kernels, leaving ~2.6 us of launch and dependency gap. The sk kernel's prologue is a serial chain: load_prefix(seqlens) -> issue_meta (page_table) -> cp.async of K/V tiles, two dependent DRAM round trips (~1-1.5 us) before the first byte of KV arrives. Running that chain under pre-attention is a real saving. WEAKEST LINK: without griddepcontrol.launch_dependents in the primary, the dependent is released only when every primary CTA has exited. The overlap is then the dependent's launch latency and the primary's tail/flush (~0.5-1 us), not the 1.4 us body. splitkv-pdl-attn-to-combine (neutral, same environment) is the precedent for a sub-noise PDL gain. An explicit trigger at the top of _pre_attention_kernel (Triton gdc_launch_dependents if this Triton has it, else tl.inline_asm_elementwise('griddepcontrol.launch_dependents;')) lets the index chain overlap the body. It is a no-op for any dependent launched without the PDL attribute, so every other shape is unaffected.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (landed c3c1b01): the dependent is its variant-3 kernel at grid SM. The change touches only the B=1 launch, so read the full decode_1 row and the sk kernel row. The kernel row should not change; the shape row should drop.

fused-preattention-triton (landed): this is the primary. If an explicit trigger is added, the kernel changes for every shape (benign no-op). Check that sliding decode rows (which do not run it) and the other full rows stay flat.

In flight: full-decode1-sk4-cluster-dsmem-merge (queued) changes the same B=1 launch to a cluster launch. Run against master each is attributable on its own; a later stack needs both attributes on one cudaLaunchKernelEx. full-decode-splitkv-s3-fused-preattn (running) removes pre-attn at B>1 only, so it does not overlap.
interference: No companion. The prepare prints pre-attn+kernel with and without PDL (and with the explicit-trigger variant, see open_questions) on the same input. PATH CHOSEN names the variant, so a gain or flat on full decode_1 is attributable. A separate control check would only repeat the prepare.
rules_flags: Data dependency (correct as written): pre-attention writes q (all 16 heads) and cache row cache_loc[0] = position seq_lens[0] = key seq_b-1 (seq_b = cache_seqlens[0]). Everything before griddepcontrol.wait may read only page_table, cache_seqlens and KV rows < seq_b-1. The tile containing key seq_b-1 and the q load go after the wait. All rows read before the wait were written by work completed before the primary started.

q is currently loaded INSIDE issue_tile (cp_async16 of q when nn==0 || lt==0, in the same cp.async group as the first tile). The builder must move the q copy out of the pre-wait tiles into its own post-wait copy (its own cp.async group or a direct load) and keep the cp.async.wait_group counts correct. Otherwise q is read before the primary has written it, a race the self-check may not catch every time.
Workspace, ticket and gticket writes after the wait (as stated). The previous replay's kernel completed before this replay's primary started, so there is no cross-replay hazard.
Fallback to plain launch on any error is fine. The choice must be fixed at import, not per call.
